public_rationale: In his 8 April 2026 post, Zitron reports on his own search. He says he does not 'see much evidence' of Anthropic custom integrations that 'actually matter'. He also says he has found no 'real examples' of businesses using Claude other than 'vague partnerships'. What he saw cannot be checked from outside. Treating his words as the claim that no such examples exist would change what he said. Even that version depends on his own undefined tests of 'real', 'matter' and 'vague'. Some public accounts of business use came before the post. On 13 February 2026, American Banker reported that Goldman Sachs uses Claude agents to review documents, extract entities and make know-your-customer decisions (e1). The same report says 'many proofs of concept are in the works throughout Goldman' (e2). Whether accounts like these meet his standard is his own judgment, not a fact anyone can check. So the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: Only one dated public account, the American Banker report on Goldman Sachs, was examined. Anthropic's customer-story pages were not checked one by one for dates before the post.
The evidence does not show whether the Goldman trade accounting and onboarding agents were in production or still at the proof-of-concept stage.
The cited evidence does not show how Zitron himself judged the Goldman account or any other account.
The context items show that some public accounts existed. They do not test what the speaker saw or how he weighed it.

Conclusion: not checkable as stated. Scored not_adjudicable.
